declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.diag_Rop
declarations.doc: The diagonal of {lit}`R_{u,f} a` is {lit}`x ↦ ∫₀¹ a(S(t)x,…,S(t)x) dt`.
declarations.signature:
lemma diag_Rop (u : X) (f : StrongDual 𝕜 X) (a : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 n) (x : X) :
    diag (Rop u f a) x = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, a (fun _ => substOp f u t x)
declarations.source:
lemma diag_Rop (u : X) (f : StrongDual 𝕜 X) (a : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 n) (x : X) :
    diag (Rop u f a) x = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, a (fun _ => substOp f u t x) := by
  classical
  rw [Rop, diag_symmetrize, diag_apply]
  have hexp : ∀ t : ℝ, a (fun _ => substOp f u t x) =
      ∑ s : Finset (Fin n), ((((1 - t) ^ s.card * t ^ (n - s.card) : ℝ)) : 𝕜) *
        a (s.piecewise (fun _ => x) (fun _ => f x • u)) := by
    intro t
    have : (fun _ : Fin n => substOp f u t x) =
        fun _ => ((1 - t : ℝ) : 𝕜) • x + ((t : ℝ) : 𝕜) • (f x • u) := by
      funext; rw [substOp_apply]
    rw [this, map_convex_expand]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun s _ => ?_
    push_cast
    rfl
  simp_rw [hexp]
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_finsetSum]
  · simp only [_root_.sum_apply, smul_apply,
      ContinuousMultilinearMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun s _ => ?_
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_mul_const, RCLike.intervalIntegral_ofReal, betaW]
    congr 2
    funext i
    by_cases hi : i ∈ s <;> simp [Finset.piecewise, hi]
  · intro s _
    apply Continuous.intervalIntegrable
    fun_prop

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.norm_integral_diag_le
declarations.signature:
lemma norm_integral_diag_le (a : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 n) {f : StrongDual 𝕜 X} {u : X} (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1)
    (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) {x : X} (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ 1) :
    ‖∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, a (fun _ => substOp f u t x)‖ ≤ polyNorm (diag a)
declarations.source:
lemma norm_integral_diag_le (a : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 n) {f : StrongDual 𝕜 X} {u : X} (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1)
    (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) {x : X} (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ 1) :
    ‖∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, a (fun _ => substOp f u t x)‖ ≤ polyNorm (diag a) := by
  have := intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const (a := 0) (b := 1)
    (f := fun t => a (fun _ => substOp f u t x)) (C := polyNorm (diag a)) (by
      intro t ht
      rw [Set.uIoc_of_le zero_le_one] at ht
      exact norm_diag_le_polyNorm a ((norm_substOp_le hf hu ht.1.le ht.2 x).trans hx))
  simpa using this

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.polyNorm_Rop_le
declarations.signature:
lemma polyNorm_Rop_le (a : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 n) {f : StrongDual 𝕜 X} {u : X} (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1)
    (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) : polyNorm (diag (Rop u f a)) ≤ polyNorm (diag a)
declarations.source:
lemma polyNorm_Rop_le (a : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 n) {f : StrongDual 𝕜 X} {u : X} (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1)
    (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) : polyNorm (diag (Rop u f a)) ≤ polyNorm (diag a) := by
  apply polyNorm_le (polyNorm_nonneg _)
  intro x hx
  rw [diag_Rop]
  exact norm_integral_diag_le a hf hu hx

declarations.signature:
lemma diag_Rop_fix (a : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 n) {f : StrongDual 𝕜 X} {u : X} (hfu : f u = 1) :

declarations.source:
lemma diag_Rop_fix (a : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 n) {f : StrongDual 𝕜 X} {u : X} (hfu : f u = 1) :

  rw [diag_Rop]
  simp only [substOp_fix hfu]

lemma re_integral_diag (a : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 n) (f : StrongDual 𝕜 X) (u x : X) :

lemma isHomPoly_comp {n : ℕ} {P : X → Y} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) (g : StrongDual 𝕜 Y) :

declarations.signature:
lemma norm_abExtV_le {n : ℕ} {P : X → Y} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) {z : Bidual 𝕜 X}
    (hz : ‖z‖ ≤ 1) : ‖abExtV 𝕜 n P z‖ ≤ polyNorm P
declarations.source:
lemma norm_abExtV_le {n : ℕ} {P : X → Y} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) {z : Bidual 𝕜 X}
    (hz : ‖z‖ ≤ 1) : ‖abExtV 𝕜 n P z‖ ≤ polyNorm P := by
  have h := norm_diagExtV_le (isSymm_symmForm (𝕜 := 𝕜) (n := n) P) z hz

lemma abExtV_inclusion {n : ℕ} {P : X → Y} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) (x : X) :

declarations.source:
lemma abExtV_inclusion {n : ℕ} {P : X → Y} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) (x : X) :
    abExtV 𝕜 n P (NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 X x) =
      NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 Y (P x) := by
  ext g
  rw [abExtV_apply hP, abExt_inclusion (isHomPoly_comp hP g), NormedSpace.dual_def]

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.polyNorm_abExtV
declarations.signature:
theorem polyNorm_abExtV {n : ℕ} {P : X → Y} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) :
    polyNorm (abExtV 𝕜 n P) = polyNorm P
declarations.source:
theorem polyNorm_abExtV {n : ℕ} {P : X → Y} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) :
    polyNorm (abExtV 𝕜 n P) = polyNorm P := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact polyNorm_le (polyNorm_nonneg _) fun z hz => norm_abExtV_le hP hz
  · apply polyNorm_le (polyNorm_nonneg _)
    intro x hx
    have h := norm_le_polyNorm (P := abExtV 𝕜 n P) (fun z hz => norm_abExtV_le hP hz)
      ((NormedSpace.double_dual_bound 𝕜 X x).trans hx)
    have e : ‖NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 Y (P x)‖ = ‖P x‖ :=
      (NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDualLi 𝕜 (E := Y)).norm_map (P x)
    rwa [abExtV_inclusion hP, e] at h

lemma norm_abExt_le {n : ℕ} {P : X → 𝕜} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) {z : Bidual 𝕜 X}

lemma norm_abExt_le {n : ℕ} {P : X → 𝕜} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) {z : Bidual 𝕜 X}

theorem polyNorm_abExt {n : ℕ} {P : X → 𝕜} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) :

theorem polyNorm_abExt {n : ℕ} {P : X → 𝕜} (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) :
    polyNorm (abExt 𝕜 n P) = polyNorm P := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact polyNorm_le (polyNorm_nonneg _) fun z hz => norm_abExt_le hP hz

    have h := norm_le_polyNorm (P := abExt 𝕜 n P) (fun z hz => norm_abExt_le hP hz)
      ((NormedSpace.double_dual_bound 𝕜 X x).trans hx)
    rwa [abExt_inclusion hP] at h

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.norm_diagExtV_scalar
declarations.doc: For scalar-valued forms, the vector-valued extension has the same modulus.
declarations.signature:
lemma norm_diagExtV_scalar {m : ℕ} (z : Bidual 𝕜 X) (B : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 m) :
    ‖diagExtV z B‖ = ‖diagExt z B‖
declarations.source:
lemma norm_diagExtV_scalar {m : ℕ} (z : Bidual 𝕜 X) (B : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 m) :
    ‖diagExtV z B‖ = ‖diagExt z B‖ := by
  have hcomp : ∀ g : StrongDual 𝕜 𝕜, g.compContinuousMultilinearMap B = g 1 • B := by
    intro g
    ext v
    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.compContinuousMultilinearMap_coe, Function.comp_apply,
      smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    conv_lhs => rw [← mul_one (B v)]
    rw [← smul_eq_mul, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
  have hval : ∀ g : StrongDual 𝕜 𝕜, diagExtV z B g = g 1 * diagExt z B := by
    intro g
    rw [diagExtV_apply, hcomp, diagExt_smul]
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ (norm_nonneg _)
    intro g
    rw [hval, norm_mul, mul_comm]
    gcongr
    simpa using g.le_opNorm 1
  · calc ‖diagExt z B‖ = ‖diagExtV z B (ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 𝕜)‖ := by
          rw [hval]; simp
      _ ≤ ‖diagExtV z B‖ * ‖ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 𝕜‖ := (diagExtV z B).le_opNorm _
      _ ≤ ‖diagExtV z B‖ * 1 :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
            (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_nonneg _)
      _ = _ := mul_one _

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.norm_abExtV_scalar
declarations.signature:
lemma norm_abExtV_scalar {n : ℕ} (P : X → 𝕜) (z : Bidual 𝕜 X) :
    ‖abExtV 𝕜 n P z‖ = ‖abExt 𝕜 n P z‖
declarations.source:
lemma norm_abExtV_scalar {n : ℕ} (P : X → 𝕜) (z : Bidual 𝕜 X) :
    ‖abExtV 𝕜 n P z‖ = ‖abExt 𝕜 n P z‖ :=
  norm_diagExtV_scalar z _

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.norm_smul_bidual
declarations.signature: lemma norm_smul_bidual {c : 𝕜} (hc : c ≠ 0) (T : Bidual 𝕜 Y) : ‖c • T‖ = ‖c‖ * ‖T‖
declarations.source:
lemma norm_smul_bidual {c : 𝕜} (hc : c ≠ 0) (T : Bidual 𝕜 Y) : ‖c • T‖ = ‖c‖ * ‖T‖ := by
  apply le_antisymm (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_smul_le c T)
  have h := ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_smul_le c⁻¹ (c • T)
  rw [inv_smul_smul₀ hc, norm_inv] at h
  have hcpos : 0 < ‖c‖ := norm_pos_iff.mpr hc
  calc ‖c‖ * ‖T‖ ≤ ‖c‖ * (‖c‖⁻¹ * ‖c • T‖) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h hcpos.le
    _ = ‖c • T‖ := by field_simp

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.polyNorm_zero_fun
declarations.signature: lemma polyNorm_zero_fun : polyNorm (0 : X → Y) = 0
declarations.source:
lemma polyNorm_zero_fun : polyNorm (0 : X → Y) = 0 :=
  le_antisymm (polyNorm_le le_rfl fun x _ => by simp) (polyNorm_nonneg _)

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.polynomial_lindenstrauss_vector
declarations.doc:
**Theorem {lit}`thm:vector`** (polynomial Lindenstrauss theorem, vector-valued).
For every continuous {lit}`n`-homogeneous polynomial {lit}`P : X → Y` ({lit}`n ≥ 1`, {lit}`Y` complete) and
every {lit}`ε > 0` there are a continuous {lit}`n`-homogeneous polynomial {lit}`Q` with {lit}`‖Q - P‖ < ε` and
a point {lit}`z` of the closed unit ball of {lit}`X**` with {lit}`‖Q̃(z)‖ = ‖Q̃‖ = ‖Q‖`.
declarations.signature:
theorem polynomial_lindenstrauss_vector [CompleteSpace Y] {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {P : X → Y}
    (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ Q : X → Y, IsHomPoly 𝕜 n Q ∧ polyNorm (Q - P) < ε ∧
      ∃ z : Bidual 𝕜 X, ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧
        ‖abExtV 𝕜 n Q z‖ = polyNorm (abExtV 𝕜 n Q) ∧ polyNorm (abExtV 𝕜 n Q) = polyNorm Q
declarations.source:
theorem polynomial_lindenstrauss_vector [CompleteSpace Y] {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {P : X → Y}
    (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ Q : X → Y, IsHomPoly 𝕜 n Q ∧ polyNorm (Q - P) < ε ∧
      ∃ z : Bidual 𝕜 X, ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧
        ‖abExtV 𝕜 n Q z‖ = polyNorm (abExtV 𝕜 n Q) ∧ polyNorm (abExtV 𝕜 n Q) = polyNorm Q := by
  obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ : ∃ d, n = d + 1 := ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
  set S := symmForm 𝕜 (d + 1) P with hSdef
  have hS : IsSymm S := isSymm_symmForm P
  have hSP : diag S = P := diag_symmForm hP
  set p := polyNorm P with hpdef
  have hp0 : 0 ≤ p := polyNorm_nonneg _
  rcases hp0.eq_or_lt with hp | hp
  · -- `P = 0` in norm: take `Q = P` and `z = 0`
    have hz0 : ‖(0 : Bidual 𝕜 X)‖ ≤ 1 :=
      ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ zero_le_one (fun g => by simp)
    refine ⟨P, hP, by rw [sub_self, polyNorm_zero_fun]; exact hε, 0, hz0, ?_,
      polyNorm_abExtV hP⟩
    rw [polyNorm_abExtV hP]
    have h0 := norm_abExtV_le hP hz0
    have hP0 : polyNorm P = 0 := hp.symm
    rw [hP0] at h0 ⊢
    exact le_antisymm h0 (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_nonneg _)
  · have : Nontrivial X := by
      by_contra hX
      rw [not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton] at hX
      have : p ≤ 0 := polyNorm_le le_rfl fun x _ => by
        rw [Subsingleton.elim x 0, ← hSP]
        simp only [diag_apply]
        rw [S.map_coord_zero 0 rfl, norm_zero]
      linarith
    set A : MLin 𝕜 X Y (d + 1) := ((p⁻¹ : ℝ) : 𝕜) • S with hAdef
    have hA : IsSymm A := hS.smul _
    have hA1 : polyNorm (diag A) = 1 := by
      rw [hAdef, polyNorm_diag_smul, hSP, RCLike.norm_ofReal, abs_inv, abs_of_pos hp,
        inv_mul_cancel₀ hp.ne']
    obtain ⟨B, hB, hBA, z, hz, hatt⟩ := core_attain hA hA1 (div_pos hε hp)
    have hpS : ((p : ℝ) : 𝕜) • A = S := by
      rw [hAdef, smul_smul, ← RCLike.ofReal_mul, mul_inv_cancel₀ hp.ne', RCLike.ofReal_one,
        one_smul]
    set Q := diag (((p : ℝ) : 𝕜) • B) with hQdef
    have hQ : IsHomPoly 𝕜 (d + 1) Q := isHomPoly_diag _
    have hsQ : symmForm 𝕜 (d + 1) Q = ((p : ℝ) : 𝕜) • B :=
      symmForm_eq_of_isSymm (hB.smul _)
    have hnp : ‖((p : ℝ) : 𝕜)‖ = p := by rw [RCLike.norm_ofReal, abs_of_pos hp]
    refine ⟨Q, hQ, ?_, z, hz, ?_, polyNorm_abExtV hQ⟩
    · have : Q - P = diag (((p : ℝ) : 𝕜) • (B - A)) := by
        rw [smul_sub, hpS, diag_sub, hSP]
      rw [this, polyNorm_diag_smul, hnp]
      calc p * polyNorm (diag (B - A)) < p * (ε / p) := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hBA hp
        _ = ε := by field_simp
    · rw [polyNorm_abExtV hQ, abExtV, hsQ, diagExtV_smul,
        norm_smul_bidual (by exact_mod_cast hp.ne'), hnp, hatt, hQdef, polyNorm_diag_smul, hnp]

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.polynomial_lindenstrauss
declarations.doc:
**Theorem {lit}`thm:main`** (polynomial Lindenstrauss theorem, scalar-valued; {lit}`𝕜 = ℝ` or {lit}`ℂ`).
For every continuous {lit}`n`-homogeneous polynomial {lit}`P : X → 𝕜` ({lit}`n ≥ 1`) and every {lit}`ε > 0`
there are a continuous {lit}`n`-homogeneous polynomial {lit}`Q` with {lit}`‖Q - P‖ < ε` and a point {lit}`z`
of the closed unit ball of {lit}`X**` with {lit}`|Q̃(z)| = ‖Q̃‖ = ‖Q‖`.
declarations.signature:
theorem polynomial_lindenstrauss {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {P : X → 𝕜}
    (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ Q : X → 𝕜, IsHomPoly 𝕜 n Q ∧ polyNorm (Q - P) < ε ∧
      ∃ z : Bidual 𝕜 X, ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧
        ‖abExt 𝕜 n Q z‖ = polyNorm (abExt 𝕜 n Q) ∧ polyNorm (abExt 𝕜 n Q) = polyNorm Q
declarations.source:
theorem polynomial_lindenstrauss {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {P : X → 𝕜}
    (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ Q : X → 𝕜, IsHomPoly 𝕜 n Q ∧ polyNorm (Q - P) < ε ∧
      ∃ z : Bidual 𝕜 X, ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧
        ‖abExt 𝕜 n Q z‖ = polyNorm (abExt 𝕜 n Q) ∧ polyNorm (abExt 𝕜 n Q) = polyNorm Q := by
  obtain ⟨Q, hQ, hQP, z, hz, h1, h2⟩ := polynomial_lindenstrauss_vector hn hP hε
  refine ⟨Q, hQ, hQP, z, hz, ?_, polyNorm_abExt hQ⟩
  rw [polyNorm_abExt hQ, ← norm_abExtV_scalar, h1, h2]

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.polynomial_lindenstrauss_dense
declarations.doc:
The density formulation of Theorem {lit}`thm:main`: every continuous {lit}`n`-homogeneous scalar
polynomial is a limit, in the norm {lit}`‖·‖`, of polynomials whose canonical extensions attain
their norms.
declarations.signature:
theorem polynomial_lindenstrauss_dense {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {P : X → 𝕜}
    (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) :
    ∃ Q : ℕ → X → 𝕜, (∀ k, IsHomPoly 𝕜 n (Q k) ∧
        ∃ z : Bidual 𝕜 X, ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧ ‖abExt 𝕜 n (Q k) z‖ = polyNorm (abExt 𝕜 n (Q k))) ∧
      Tendsto (fun k => polyNorm (Q k - P)) atTop (𝓝 0)
declarations.source:
theorem polynomial_lindenstrauss_dense {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {P : X → 𝕜}
    (hP : IsHomPoly 𝕜 n P) :
    ∃ Q : ℕ → X → 𝕜, (∀ k, IsHomPoly 𝕜 n (Q k) ∧
        ∃ z : Bidual 𝕜 X, ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧ ‖abExt 𝕜 n (Q k) z‖ = polyNorm (abExt 𝕜 n (Q k))) ∧
      Tendsto (fun k => polyNorm (Q k - P)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  choose Q hQ hQP z hz h1 _ using fun k : ℕ =>
    polynomial_lindenstrauss hn hP (Nat.one_div_pos_of_nat (n := k) (α := ℝ))
  refine ⟨Q, fun k => ⟨hQ k, z k, hz k, h1 k⟩, ?_⟩
  refine squeeze_zero (fun k => polyNorm_nonneg _) (fun k => (hQP k).le) ?_
  exact tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.tendsto_ulim
declarations.signature:
lemma tendsto_ulim {s : ℕ → 𝕜} {R : ℝ} (hs : ∀ k, ‖s k‖ ≤ R) :
    Tendsto s (𝒰 : Filter ℕ) (𝓝 (ulim s))
declarations.source:
lemma tendsto_ulim {s : ℕ → 𝕜} {R : ℝ} (hs : ∀ k, ‖s k‖ ≤ R) :
    Tendsto s (𝒰 : Filter ℕ) (𝓝 (ulim s)) := by
  apply tendsto_nhds_limUnder
  obtain ⟨x, -, hx⟩ := (isCompact_closedBall (0 : 𝕜) R).ultrafilter_le_nhds (𝒰.map s) (by
    rw [Ultrafilter.coe_map, le_principal_iff]
    exact Filter.mem_map.mpr (Filter.univ_mem' fun k => by simpa using hs k))
  exact ⟨x, hx⟩

lemma eventually_gt_ultra (N : ℕ) : ∀ᶠ k in (𝒰 : Filter ℕ), N < k :=
  (eventually_gt_atTop N).filter_mono (hyperfilter_le_cofinite.trans Nat.cofinite_eq_atTop.le)

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.ultraPoint
declarations.signature: def ultraPoint (x : ℕ → X) (hx : ∀ k, ‖x k‖ ≤ 1) : Bidual 𝕜 X
declarations.source:
def ultraPoint (x : ℕ → X) (hx : ∀ k, ‖x k‖ ≤ 1) : Bidual 𝕜 X :=
  LinearMap.mkContinuous
    { toFun := fun f => ulim (fun k => f (x k))
      map_add' := fun f g => by
        have hf := tendsto_ulim (s := fun k => f (x k)) (R := ‖f‖) (fun k =>
          (f.le_opNorm _).trans (by simpa using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hx k) (norm_nonneg f)))
        have hg := tendsto_ulim (s := fun k => g (x k)) (R := ‖g‖) (fun k =>
          (g.le_opNorm _).trans (by simpa using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hx k) (norm_nonneg g)))
        have hfg := tendsto_ulim (s := fun k => (f + g) (x k)) (R := ‖f + g‖) (fun k =>
          ((f + g).le_opNorm _).trans
            (by simpa using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hx k) (norm_nonneg (f + g))))
        exact tendsto_nhds_unique hfg (by simpa using hf.add hg)
      map_smul' := fun c f => by
        have hf := tendsto_ulim (s := fun k => f (x k)) (R := ‖f‖) (fun k =>
          (f.le_opNorm _).trans (by simpa using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hx k) (norm_nonneg f)))
        have hcf := tendsto_ulim (s := fun k => (c • f) (x k)) (R := ‖c • f‖) (fun k =>
          ((c • f).le_opNorm _).trans
            (by simpa using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hx k) (norm_nonneg (c • f))))
        exact tendsto_nhds_unique hcf (by simpa using hf.const_mul c) }
    1
    (fun f => by
      simp only [LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, one_mul]
      have hb : ∀ k, ‖f (x k)‖ ≤ ‖f‖ := fun k =>
        (f.le_opNorm _).trans (by simpa using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hx k) (norm_nonneg f))
      have hf := tendsto_ulim hb
      exact le_of_tendsto hf.norm (Filter.Eventually.of_forall hb))

lemma ultraPoint_apply (x : ℕ → X) (hx : ∀ k, ‖x k‖ ≤ 1) (f : StrongDual 𝕜 X) :

declarations.source:
lemma ultraPoint_apply (x : ℕ → X) (hx : ∀ k, ‖x k‖ ≤ 1) (f : StrongDual 𝕜 X) :

  LinearMap.mkContinuous_norm_le _ zero_le_one _

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.strictMono_snoc
declarations.signature:
lemma strictMono_snoc {r : ℕ} {ι : Fin r → ℕ} (hι : StrictMono ι) {k : ℕ}
    (hk : ∀ i, ι i < k) : StrictMono (Fin.snoc ι k : Fin (r + 1) → ℕ)
declarations.source:
lemma strictMono_snoc {r : ℕ} {ι : Fin r → ℕ} (hι : StrictMono ι) {k : ℕ}
    (hk : ∀ i, ι i < k) : StrictMono (Fin.snoc ι k : Fin (r + 1) → ℕ) := by
  intro a b hab
  induction b using Fin.lastCases with
  | last =>
    induction a using Fin.lastCases with
    | last => exact absurd hab (lt_irrefl _)
    | cast a => simpa using hk a
  | cast b =>
    induction a using Fin.lastCases with
    | last => exact absurd hab (not_lt.mpr (Fin.le_last _))
    | cast a =>
      simp only [Fin.snoc_castSucc]
      exact hι (Fin.castSucc_lt_castSucc_iff.mp hab)

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.strictMono_cons
declarations.signature:
lemma strictMono_cons {r : ℕ} {ι : Fin r → ℕ} (hι : StrictMono ι) {m : ℕ}
    (hm : ∀ i, m < ι i) : StrictMono (Fin.cons m ι : Fin (r + 1) → ℕ)
declarations.source:
lemma strictMono_cons {r : ℕ} {ι : Fin r → ℕ} (hι : StrictMono ι) {m : ℕ}
    (hm : ∀ i, m < ι i) : StrictMono (Fin.cons m ι : Fin (r + 1) → ℕ) := by
  intro a b hab
  induction b using Fin.cases with
  | zero => exact absurd hab (not_lt.mpr (Fin.zero_le _))
  | succ b =>
    induction a using Fin.cases with
    | zero => simpa using hm b
    | succ a =>
      simp only [Fin.cons_succ]
      exact hι (Fin.succ_lt_succ_iff.mp hab)

declarations.name: LindenstraussPolynomials.le_norm_diagExt_ultra
declarations.doc:
Lower bounds at strictly increasing tuples of indices larger than {lit}`m` survive the
iterated limits defining the canonical extension at the ultrafilter limit point.
declarations.signature:
theorem le_norm_diagExt_ultra (x : ℕ → X) (hx : ∀ k, ‖x k‖ ≤ 1) (m : ℕ) (β : ℝ) :
    ∀ {r : ℕ} (C : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 r),
      (∀ ι : Fin r → ℕ, StrictMono ι → (∀ i, m < ι i) → β ≤ ‖C (fun i => x (ι i))‖) →
      β ≤ ‖diagExt (ultraPoint x hx) C‖
  | 0, C, h => by
    have
declarations.source:
theorem le_norm_diagExt_ultra (x : ℕ → X) (hx : ∀ k, ‖x k‖ ≤ 1) (m : ℕ) (β : ℝ) :
    ∀ {r : ℕ} (C : MLin 𝕜 X 𝕜 r),
      (∀ ι : Fin r → ℕ, StrictMono ι → (∀ i, m < ι i) → β ≤ ‖C (fun i => x (ι i))‖) →
      β ≤ ‖diagExt (ultraPoint x hx) C‖
  | 0, C, h => by
    have := h (fun i => Fin.elim0 i) (fun i => Fin.elim0 i) (fun i => Fin.elim0 i)
    simp only [diagExt_zero]
    convert this using 3
  | r + 1, C, h => by
    rw [diagExt_succ]
    apply le_norm_diagExt_ultra x hx m β (extLast _ C)
    intro ι hι hm
    rw [extLast_apply, ultraPoint_apply]
    set s : ℕ → 𝕜 := fun k => C.curryRight (fun i => x (ι i)) (x k)
    have hb : ∀ k, ‖s k‖ ≤ ‖C.curryRight (fun i => x (ι i))‖ := fun k =>
      ((C.curryRight _).le_opNorm _).trans (by
        simpa using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hx k) (norm_nonneg _))
    have hs := tendsto_ulim hb
    apply ge_of_tendsto hs.norm
    filter_upwards [eventually_gt_ultra (m + ∑ i, ι i)] with k hk
    simp only [s, curryRight_apply']
    have hk' : ∀ i, ι i < k := fun i => by
      have : ι i ≤ ∑ j, ι j :=
        Finset.single_le_sum (f := ι) (fun j _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Finset.mem_univ i)
      omega
    have := h (Fin.snoc ι k) (strictMono_snoc hι hk') (fun i => by
      induction i using Fin.lastCases with
      | last => simp only [Fin.snoc_last]; omega
      | cast i => simpa using hm i)
    convert this using 3
    funext i
    induction i using Fin.lastCases with
    | last => simp
    | cast i => simp

abstract: We establish a polynomial analogue of Lindenstrauss' theorem in full generality. More precisely, we prove that, for every real or complex Banach space \(X\) and every positive integer \(n\), the \(n\)-homogeneous scalar-valued polynomials whose Aron–Berner extensions to \(X^{**}\) attain their norms form a dense subset of \(\mathcal P({}^n X)\). This resolves a problem posed by Aron, García and Maestre in 2003, extending their result for quadratic polynomials to arbitrary degrees without imposing any structural assumptions on the underlying Banach space. We further establish the corresponding theorem for vector-valued polynomials with arbitrary Banach space codomains. Our approach relies on a new perturbation scheme based on averaged linear contractions, which provides simultaneous control of the multilinear variables and yields norm attainment through iterated limits in the bidual.
context: A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of the article *Density of polynomials whose Aron–Berner extensions attain their norms* by J. Falcó. Every result below is proved without {lit}`sorry` and depends only on the standard axioms {lit}`propext`, {lit}`Classical.choice` and {lit}`Quot.sound`. The scalar field is any {lit}`RCLike` field, so each statement holds over $`\mathbb R` and over $`\mathbb C`.

steps.title: Homogeneous polynomials
steps.intro: Throughout, $`\mathbb K` is $`\mathbb R` or $`\mathbb C` (an {lit}`RCLike` field) and $`X`, $`Y` are normed spaces over $`\mathbb K`. A continuous $`n`-homogeneous polynomial $`P\colon X\to Y` is a map of the form $`P(x)=L(x,\ldots,x)` for some continuous $`n`-linear map $`L` ({lit}`IsHomPoly`). Its norm is the supremum over the closed unit ball, $$`\|P\| = \sup_{\|x\|\le 1}\|P(x)\|` ({lit}`polyNorm`). This module collects the elementary facts about diagonals of multilinear maps and their symmetrizations used everywhere else.

steps.title: Polarization
steps.intro:
The identities of Section 1 of the article that recover the symmetric form $`\check P` from the polynomial $`P`:

* the finite-difference polarization formula ({lit}`eq:finitepolar`) and the sign polarization formula ({lit}`eq:signpolar`); * the estimate $`\|P\|\le\|\check P\|\le c_n\|P\|` with $`c_n=n^n/n!` ({lit}`eq:polarnorm`); * the uniqueness of the symmetric form with a given diagonal; * the Lipschitz estimate $`|P(x)-P(y)|\le n c_n\|P\|\,\|x-y\|` on the unit ball ({lit}`eq:lipschitz`).

steps.title: The canonical (Aron–Berner) extension
steps.intro: For $`z\in X^{**}` and a continuous $`(m+1)`-linear form $`C` on $`X`, one step of the extension is the $`m`-linear form $$`(v_1,\ldots,v_m)\longmapsto z\bigl(v\mapsto C(v_1,\ldots,v_m,v)\bigr)` ({lit}`eq:partial`). Iterating it $`n` times extends the last variable first and gives $`\overline A(z,\ldots,z)`, the value at the diagonal point of the canonical extension ({lit}`eq:arens`, {lit}`eq:AB`). For a vector-valued polynomial the extension $`\widetilde P\colon X^{**}\to Y^{**}` is defined by $`\widetilde P(z)(y^*)=\widetilde{y^*\circ P}(z)` ({lit}`eq:ABvector`).

steps.title: The substitutions and the averaging operators
steps.intro: For $`\|u\|=\|f\|=f(u)=1` and $`t\in[0,1]`, the substitution $$`S_{u,f}(t)\,x = (1-t)\,x + t\,f(x)\,u` ({lit}`eq:substitution`) maps the unit ball into itself and fixes $`u`. Averaging a polynomial over these substitutions gives $$`\mathcal R_{u,f}P(x) = \int_0^1 P\bigl(S_{u,f}(t)\,x\bigr)\,dt,` and this module proves the properties of $`\mathcal R_{u,f}` the construction needs ({lit}`eq:Rproperties`, {lit}`eq:expansion`, {lit}`eq:Rfinite`).

steps.title: Ordered compositions of substitutions
steps.intro: The composition $`S_1(t_1)\,S_2(t_2)\cdots S_d(t_d)\,x`, where $`S_i(t)\,y=(1-t)\,y+t\,f_i(y)\,u_i`. As in the article, the operators act from right to left: $`S_d(t_d)` is applied first and $`S_1(t_1)` last. Each $`S_i(t)` is a linear contraction when $`\|f_i\|\le1` and $`\|u_i\|\le1`.

steps.title: The geometric lemma (Lemma lem:geometry and Remark rem:real)
steps.intro: Let $`\|P\|\le M`, $`u_1,\ldots,u_n` in the unit ball of $`X` and $`f_1,\ldots,f_{n-1}` in the unit ball of $`X^*`. If $$`\operatorname{Re}P\bigl(S_1(t_1)\cdots S_{n-1}(t_{n-1})\,u_n\bigr)\ge M-E\quad\text{for all }t_1,\ldots,t_{n-1}\in[0,1],` then the fully mixed value of the symmetric form is almost maximal: $$`|\check P(u_1,\ldots,u_n)| \ge M - H_n\sqrt{ME}.` Over $`\mathbb R` the bound improves to $`M-C_nE` (Remark {lit}`rem:real`).

steps.title: An estimate for nonnegative polynomials (Lemma lem:K)
steps.intro:
For every $`n\ge1` there is $`K_n\ge1` such that $$`\max_{0\le t\le1} r(t) \le K_n\int_0^1 r(t)\,dt` for every real polynomial $`r` of degree at most $`n` that is nonnegative on $`[0,1]`.

The formal proof minimizes $`\int_0^1|r|` over the unit sphere of the coefficient space, which is compact; the article argues by contradiction with Vandermonde interpolation. Both prove the same statement.

steps.title: The step sizes
steps.intro: The perturbations of the construction use the step sizes $`\alpha_k=a^{2^k}` for a fixed $`a\in(0,1)`, so that $`\alpha_{k+1}=\alpha_k^2`; this identity is used essentially in the inductive step. The module proves the tail estimates ({lit}`eq:tails`) and the product estimate ({lit}`eq:product`). Indices start at $`0`: $`\alpha_0=a` is the article's $`\alpha_1`.

steps.title: Limits along an ultrafilter
steps.intro: For a sequence $`(x_k)` in the unit ball of $`X` and a free ultrafilter $`\mathcal U` on $`\mathbb N`, $`z(f)=\lim_{k\to\mathcal U}f(x_k)` defines a point $`z` of the unit ball of $`X^{**}` ({lit}`eq:z`), and the canonical extension at $`z` is an iterated limit along $`\mathcal U` ({lit}`eq:ulpartial`). Lower bounds that hold at every strictly increasing tuple of indices survive these limits.

steps.title: The perturbation scheme
steps.intro: Starting from $`P_0=P`, the construction ({lit}`eq:viteration`) sets $$`P_{k+1} = P_k + \alpha_k\,(\mathcal R_k p_k)\,w_k,\qquad p_k=y_k^*\circ P_k,\quad w_k=\frac{P_k(x_k)}{\|P_k(x_k)\|},` where $`x_k` almost norms $`P_k`, $`f_k` is a norming functional of $`x_k`, and $`y_k^*` norms $`P_k(x_k)`. Polynomials are represented by their symmetric $`n`-linear forms. The module proves the norm increments ({lit}`eq:increment`) and bounds ({lit}`eq:normbounds`).

steps.title: The limit polynomial
steps.intro: The perturbations are summable: $`\|P_m-P_k\|\le 2\alpha_k/(1-a)`, so $`(P_k)` converges to a symmetric form $`Q` with $`\|Q-P_k\|\le4\alpha_k` ({lit}`eq:tailQ`).

steps.title: Deficits
steps.intro: The deficits $`d_k^g(y)=M_k-\operatorname{Re}g(P_k\,y)` and the losses $`\lambda_k=(1+\alpha_k)M_k-M_{k+1}` satisfy an exact identity under the perturbation ({lit}`eq:vdeficit`); from it come the backward estimate ({lit}`eq:vbackward`), the insertion estimate ({lit}`eq:vinsert`) and the bound on the losses ({lit}`eq:loss`).

steps.title: Control of ordered compositions
steps.intro: Iterating the deficit identity controls the deficits along ordered compositions of substitutions ({lit}`eq:vbase`, {lit}`eq:vcompositions`), with a bound $`(7K_n)^d\alpha_{i_1}` and a scalar that does not depend on the parameters $`t_i` — which is what Lemma {lit}`lem:geometry` needs.

steps.title: Norm preservation (Lemma lem:isometry)
steps.intro:
The theorem of Davie and Gamelin: for a symmetric $`n`-linear form $`a` and $`z` in the closed unit ball of $`X^{**}`, $$`|\overline a(z,\ldots,z)| \le \sup_{\|x\|\le1}|a(x,\ldots,x)|,` so the canonical extension preserves the norm of a polynomial.

The proof follows Davie and Gamelin: points of the unit ball of $`X` are chosen one at a time, by a finite-dimensional form of Goldstine's theorem, so that every increasing tuple of chosen points approximates the iterated extension; the polynomial is then evaluated at averages of the chosen points. It uses only multilinearity, so it works over $`\mathbb R` as well as over $`\mathbb C`, as the article remarks.

steps.title: The core of the proof
steps.intro: For every increasing $`n`-tuple of almost norming points the geometric lemma gives a lower bound for the fully mixed value of the limit form ({lit}`eq:vordered`); iterated limits along an ultrafilter then turn these bounds into $`\|\widetilde Q(z)\|\ge\|Q\|` at a point $`z` of the unit ball of $`X^{**}`.

steps.title: Main results
steps.intro:
* Lemma {lit}`lem:isometry`: the canonical extension preserves the norm, for scalar- and vector-valued polynomials. * Theorem {lit}`thm:main`: for every continuous $`n`-homogeneous scalar polynomial $`P` ($`n\ge1`) and every $`\varepsilon>0` there are $`Q` and $`z` in the unit ball of $`X^{**}` with $`\|Q-P\|<\varepsilon` and $`|\widetilde Q(z)|=\|\widetilde Q\|=\|Q\|`; equivalently, such polynomials are dense. * Theorem {lit}`thm:vector`: the same for polynomials with values in a Banach space $`Y`.

Here $`\|\widetilde Q\|` is the supremum of $`\|\widetilde Q(z)\|` over the closed unit ball of the bidual. $`X` need not be complete; only $`Y` is assumed complete in the vector-valued case.
